picks.headline: AI May Be Making Publishing Easier, But It's Still Not Easy
picks.excerpt: Report from the July 22 Media Transformation Summit: AI is streamlining production workflows (one founder used AI in place of a traditional production team to publish 322 books) and AI systems now favor content with machine-friendly structure, pushing publishers to rethink how they present plot summaries, bios and images. A concrete look at how generative AI is reshaping real editorial and production craft.
picks.rationale: Most actionable: concrete editorial/production workflow shifts (machine-friendly metadata, AI-run production) that change how a publishing designer works now.

picks.headline: Substack adds AI detection tools, but creators can disable them
picks.excerpt: Substack now lets readers run Pangram to scan a post and see how much of it was likely AI-written, while giving creators the option to turn the badge off. A direct workflow/craft signal for writers and publishers navigating AI-disclosure and provenance in day-to-day authoring.
picks.rationale: New platform feature (AI-detection badge + opt-out) that directly changes provenance/disclosure decisions for anyone publishing on Substack.

picks.headline: 'Genius' novel sold in major six- and seven-figure deals at auction pulled over AI allegations
picks.excerpt: A crime novel that secured major six- and seven-figure deals in the US and UK has been withdrawn from sale after allegations that AI was used in its creation, with the agent pulling the book from circulation. A sharp real-world case of AI provenance and disclosure disrupting acquisition and editorial workflows in trade publishing.
picks.rationale: Fresh, high-stakes case of AI provenance killing a major book deal — distinct book/event from prior Daggermouth coverage, reputable trade source.

picks.headline: Researchers attempt to prove that generative AI dilutes the market for books
picks.excerpt: A new study tries to put empirical numbers on a fear authors have voiced for years: that the flood of generative-AI-written books measurably shrinks the market and attention available to human-authored work. A creative-industry counterpart to the AI-detection studies the beat already runs, framing how AI-generated output reshapes what gets read and sold.
picks.rationale: Novel empirical angle (market dilution measured, not just asserted) that reframes the commercial stakes of AI output for authors and publishers.
